technical_and_design_decisions: Use a file-system based module repository (configurable directory) to store uploaded module artifacts, rather than persisting binary content in the database, to keep deployment artifacts aligned with runtime classloading needs.
Persist module metadata (name, version, type, coordinates) in the existing relational store so the module registry can be rehydrated on server restart.
Replace the hard-coded ModuleRegistryPopulator bootstrap with a dynamic ModuleRegistryService that loads registered modules at startup and supports runtime registration/deregistration events.
Expose a multipart file upload REST endpoint (POST /modules) in the admin server, reusing Spring Boot's MultipartResolver and standard validation.
Implement the Data Flow Shell upload command as a thin client wrapper over the new REST endpoint, sharing the same error-handling and progress reporting as the existing shell commands.
Adopt Spring Cloud Stream's @EnableBinding source/sink/processor programming model for all migrated modules, replacing Spring XD's XML-based and Tap/Stream module abstractions.
Standardize migrated modules as Maven sub-modules under spring-cloud-stream-modules, each producing an executable uber-jar consumable by Spring Cloud Data Flow.
Preserve the source/sink semantics of the original Spring XD modules: jms, mail, mongo, mqtt, reactor-ip, and stdout are all sources.
Use the Spring Cloud Stream test binder for unit/integration tests of each migrated module to avoid external broker dependencies during CI.
Provide backward compatibility: modules still registered via the existing properties-based mechanism must continue to load alongside dynamically uploaded ones.
assumptions: The developer has full access to the existing Spring Cloud Data Flow, Spring Cloud Stream Modules, and Spring XD source repositories.
The build environment uses Java 17+, Maven, and the standard Spring Cloud Data Flow multi-module layout.
No new broker or external infrastructure is introduced; existing embedded test binder and Testcontainers are sufficient for testing.
Module upload accepts a single JAR artifact per request; multi-artifact (transitive dependency) uploads are out of scope for this increment.
Authentication/authorization for the upload endpoint follows the existing Spring Cloud Data Flow security configuration and does not require new auth features.
Shell command syntax mirrors existing Data Flow Shell commands (e.g., 'module upload').
Each migrated module is treated as an independent, similar-effort port; complex Spring XD-only features (e.g., custom plugins, named channels) are simplified during migration.
Documentation updates cover both the admin REST API reference and the Data Flow Shell reference; user guide updates for the new features are also included.
Code review, merge, and CI pipeline activities are implicit in the per-activity estimates and not broken out separately.
One developer performs all activities sequentially.
